name: Equipment
content:
Items that are martial, magical, highly specialized, or otherwise elevated above the level of Gratuiti provisions and gear (see Treasure & Keeping) are considered EQUIPMENT and must be purchased individually.

EQUIPMENT CONCEPTS

The category of Equipment encompasses a wide variety of weapons, armor and many other items, but all are defined within a shared set of Equipment concepts:

TYPE

An item's TYPE is its broadest category:

  • Weapon. An item designed for combat. Weapons provide engagement dice, damage dice, or both, and are subject to the weapon rules below.

  • Armor. Protective equipment worn on the body, as well as shields. Armor raises a character's base Defense, making attacks harder to land.

  • Item. Anything that isn't a weapon or armor — tools, accessories, relics and other gear. Items vary widely and are defined entirely by their individual attributes and descriptions.

SUBTYPE

An item's SUBTYPE is a finer category within its type. For weapons, subtype divides items into areas of training and groups items with similar characteristics. For armor, subtype identifies what part of the body it's worn on.

WEAPON SUBTYPES:

  • Melee. Close-quarters weapons for hand-to-hand fighting: swords, axes, clubs, daggers. Attacks made with melee weapons are considered melee weapon Attacks. They are the tools for those who close with their enemies and thrive in the push and pull of close combat.

  • Polearm. Long-hafted weapons that give their wielder a reach advantage: spears, halberds, pikes. Attacks made with polearms are considered melee weapon attacks. They suggest military training or the practical wisdom of keeping dangerous opponents at arm's length.

  • Ranged. Projectile weapons for attacking at distance: bows, crossbows, slings, javelins. Ranged weapons don't typically provide engagement dice. Attacks made with ranged weapons are considered ranged weapon attacks. They suit those who like to approach conflict from a distance.

  • Firearm. Gunpowder weapons: pistols, arquebuses, muskets. Firearms don't typically provide engagement dice. Each attack requires a reload, and they carry a risk of misfire (see Special Rules For Firearms below). Attacks made with firearms are considered ranged weapon attacks. Firearms are markers of modernity and specialized access — loud, powerful, and not universally available.

  • Special. Unconventional or hybrid weapons that don't fit neatly into other categories: nets, shuriken, kusarigama. Special weapons vary widely in their mechanics and are often specific to certain disciplines.

ARMOR SUBTYPES:

  • Head, Arms, Chest, Legs, Feet. Each armor piece covers one of these five body location slots (only one piece may be worn in each slot). All worn pieces contribute their respective Defense bonuses to your base Defense. Some armor may also offer other standing effects or effects that can be purchased with successes and/or engagement successes.

  • Shield. A held piece of armor. A shield provides a Defense bonus like any armor piece, but holding a shield occupies one hand rather than one of the body location slots.

GRADE

Weapons and pieces of armor each have a GRADE. An item's grade reflects its quality of craftsmanship and general capability. There are five grades:

  • Light. Physically light, whether by small size or delicate make.

  • Common. Solid and reliably serviceable, often of a form that is humble in origin.

  • Martial. Purpose-built for combat or skilled use.

  • Heavy. Physically heavy, whether by large size or dense material.

  • Great. Exceptionally large and/or highly specialized.

Higher-grade weapons tend toward larger engagement and damage dice and higher-grade armor tends toward a larger Defense bonus, but an unusual design, exotic material, or special purpose can enable an item to subvert these tendencies.

MAGIC OR MUNDANE

All equipment items - regardless of type, subtype and grade - are either MUNDANE or MAGIC:

  • Mundane. Non-magical equipment. The term describes origin, not importance — a mundane item can be of any quality and thus any Keeping tier. Equipment items are always mundane unless they are explicitly marked as magic.

  • Magic. Items imbued with magical properties. A magic item's effects are defined in its description and may be passive, triggered by use, activated by spending MP (see the Abilities section) or a success from a skill check, or triggered by other conditions. Magic items follow the same grade and Keeping conventions as all other equipment.

KEEPING

An item's KEEPING is its economic classification — an indicator of rarity, price and what maintaining it implies about a character's circumstances. Keeping determines the item's one-time purchase cost (see the Treasure & Keeping section).

Note that grade and Keeping are separate concepts: Grade describes an item's capability; Keeping describes its rarity and price. For example, a diamond-studded cudgel might be a Common weapon of Opulent Keeping, or a crudely-wrought breastplate might be Heavy armor of Modest Keeping.

In addition to the five tiers of Keeping defined in the Keeping section, equipment items may be of six additional Keeping tiers:

  • Uncommon (Cost: 5) - Elevated craftsmanship or unusual form.

  • Rare (Cost: 10) - Precious materials or powerful attributes.

  • Very Rare (Cost: 25) - Ancient, hard-to-find or unusually powerful.

  • Exceptional (Cost: 50) - The work of a master craftsman or imbued with great power.

  • Wondrous (Cost: 75) - Made by techniques gone from this world or from another entirely, or of unobtainable materials.

  • Singular (Cost: 100) - One-of-a-kind, peerless items.

These Keeping tiers are limited to equipment items and cannot be set as a character or Quest's Keeping.

WEIGHT

An item's WEIGHT is measured in pounds and contributes to a character's Load (see Core Stats). Carrying too much weight relative to your Endurance and BODY scores pushes you toward the Weary and Twice Weary States, applying penalties to skill checks.

Weight, as a contributor to Load, is a practical trade-off on every piece of equipment you carry. Higher-grade armor and larger weapons tend to weigh more, but items of the same grade can differ in weight depending on their materials and construction.

Note that Load is measured moment-to-moment, so you can choose to drop weighty gear to reduce your Load score in a pinch.

DESCRIPTION

An equipment item's description defines any special rules or effects it provides. Some effects are passive and always active while the item is carried, wielded or worn. Others are activated by spending MP, spending a success from a skill check, or triggered by a specific condition defined in the description.

WEAPON PROPERTIES

Some weapons have one or more of the following properties:

  • Finesse. This weapon can be used with either Strength or Dexterity for the attack roll. The choice is made each time you attack.

  • Piercing. Attacks with this weapon inflict Injury on a feat die result of 10 or Sol 🌞, rather than just Sol 🌞 (see the Combat section).

  • Thrown. This weapon can be used to attack a target within its range in addition to using it as a melee weapon. The weapon is still considered a melee weapon when it is thrown - and it still uses Strength for the attack roll - but the attack is considered a ranged attack.

  • Two-Handed. This weapon requires both hands to wield.

  • Reach. This weapon extends your base reach by the listed number of feet (see the Combat section).

IMPROVEMENTS & SUCCESSES

Some equipment items may offer IMPROVEMENTS, which can be purchased with XP and become a permanent feature of the item, just like ability improvements (see the Abilities section). They may also offer effects that can be bought with skill check successes, as well as effects that are triggered by Sol 🌞 and Morte 💀.

CULTURE OF ORIGIN

Each item has a CULTURE OF ORIGIN, which has no intrinsic mechanical effect, but which is tied to its availability for purchase and represents a character's history and self expression.

MARTIAL TRAINING

All weapons and armor require MARTIAL TRAINING to use them effectively. A character who lacks training with a given item subtype suffers a penalty:

  • Weapons: Attack rolls made with weapons of that subtype are ill-favored.

  • Armor & Shields: The item provides only half its normal Defense bonus, rounded down.

Training with a specific item subtype is granted by a character's Mestiere or by certain abilities.

BUYING, SELLING & REPAIRING EQUIPMENT

BUYING EQUIPMENT

The one-time purchase cost of an equipment item equals the cost, in Treasure, of its Keeping tier.

What items are actually for sale at a given time depends on where the character is located relative to the Cultures of the campaign world. Different equipment is available in different places, reflecting local craftsmanship, trade routes, and cultural specialties. The same kind of item made in two different places may have different mechanical traits or may only differ in style.

SELLING EQUIPMENT

Selling a piece of equipment in good repair yields half its original cost in Treasure, rounded down. A broken piece of equipment generally yields no Treasure when sold, though the GM may make exceptions in the case of rare materials or unusual circumstances.

BREAKING & REPAIRING EQUIPMENT

If an equipment item becomes broken, whether through mishap or as the result of a mechanical effect, the item no longer offers any of its mechanical benefits.

Mundane items with a Keeping of Uncommon or lower can be repaired in one of two ways:

  • A skilled craftsperson will generally repair an item for a fee of half the item's original cost.

  • If you have access to the materials and tools necessary to repair an item (per the GM), you may attempt to repair it yourself. You must spend a number of hours working on it equal to its original cost, in Treasure. At the end of that time, roll Craft against a difficulty equal to five times the item's original cost, in Treasure. On a pass, the item is repaired. On a failure, it remains broken.

For magic items or any item with a keeping of Rare or higher, repair requires specialized knowledge, rare materials, or other conditions, at the GM's discretion.

SPECIAL RULES FOR FIREARMS

In the world of Renaissance, firearms represent a new, powerful and volatile technology. Firearms can be hard to find, hard to repair and dangerous to use. The following rules apply to weapons of the firearm subtype:

  • Each time you make an attack with a firearm, you must spend a half action to reload the firearm before you may make another attack with it. You must have both hands free to reload the firearm.

  • Any time you roll Morte 💀 on an attack roll for an attack made with a firearm, the weapon misfires. Roll Injury, and you must spend an action to repair or reset the firearm before you can reload it.
